items.title: Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: "So when I went to Art Blakey and said, 'Well could I talk to you about Thelonious Monk' it wasn't secondhand information."

ctx.x: We could all have agreed twenty years ago it would never have happened. So there’s always something available. So the mentorship is different, but I think it’s still available. When musicians say for example, we don’t have the clubs like there were forty years ago. No, but look at all the various opportunities that are in the various schools and curriculums. So it seems like the clubs — there’s been a shift. I’m not going to say it’s better or worse, it’s different. And so each individual has to make it work for…

is becoming less and less of them but even still there is going to be a conduit from that person to the next person to the next person and so that’s the way you have to work it. I mean everyone doesn’t know Frank Sinatra, but there’s someone who knew him or knew — I met a woman the other night, I was in Monterey at the jazz festival — I met Louis Jordan’s widow.
